relations.note: Chimalman is Topiltzin’s mother and dies giving birth in a prominent version.
Malinalxochitl is consistently named as Copil’s mother.
She teaches Copil her magical arts and inspires his vengeance.
She educates Copil in resentment or charges him to avenge her abandonment.
Some late or regional traditions conflate Huemac with Topiltzin.

relations.myth: Successive rulers and Tula’s later collapse
relations.note: Huemac is a distinct successor or near-contemporary linked to Tula’s later collapse.

god_relations.note: Mixcoatl invades her country and shoots four arrows at her.
Mixcoatl lies with Chimalman, fathers her child, and is later called her husband.
Chimalman gives birth to Ce Acatl and dies four days later.
Chimalman conceives Quetzalcoatl after swallowing a precious greenstone.
Quilaztli-Cihuacoatl raises Chimalman's newborn after the mother dies.
Chimalma accompanies the Mexica group carrying Huitzilopochtli from Aztlan.
Huitzilopochtli is Copil’s maternal uncle.
Copil seeks vengeance against his uncle and rallies neighboring peoples.
Huitzilopochtli discovers the plot and commands Copil’s pre-emptive killing.
god_relations.source: Historia de los mexicanos por sus pinturas

god_relations.myth: Casting Copil’s heart from Quetzalcoatl’s stone seat
god_relations.note: Copil’s heart is cast near a stone associated with Quetzalcoatl’s departure.

god_relations.myth: The foundling destined to divide Tollan
god_relations.note: Huemac is described ambiguously as Tezcatlipoca’s offering, creation, or trace.
Tezcatlipoca’s deceptive female forms sexually compromise Huemac, costing him his priestly office.
Huemac tries to dispose of his disguised son-in-law in battle, but Tohueyo triumphs.
Tezcatlipoca stages lethal spectacles, deceptions, and portents that help ruin Huemac’s Tollan.
As Yaotl, he instigates war and sacrifice and separates followers during Huemac’s collapse.
Huemac serves as Quetzalcoatl’s minister before losing the office through deception.
Colonial chroniclers merge Huemac and Topiltzin Quetzalcoatl into one celibate holy ruler.
Huemac defeats the Tlaloque at ball and demands literal jade and quetzal feathers.
The Tlaloque withhold rain, greenness, and maize after Huemac rejects their agricultural payment.
Tlaloc’s underwater priest restores maize and conveys the demand for Quetzalxotzin’s sacrifice.
Tótec’s first wearing of human skin is placed within Huemac’s destructive reign.
Malinalxochitl is consistently described as Huitzilopochtli’s elder sister.
god_relations.source: Durán; Tovar; Crónica mexicana; Crónica Mexicayotl

god_relations.note: Huitzilopochtli directs the migrants to depart secretly while Malinalxochitl sleeps.

god_relations.myth: Comparison of Huitzilopochtli’s hostile elder sisters
god_relations.note: León-Portilla and later retellings equate them through structural analogy, not early testimony.
Modern pantheon-building calls Malinalxochitl her daughter, but core narratives provide no parentage.
Mixcoatl is Topiltzin’s father in the Leyenda genealogy.

god_relations.myth: Topiltzin recovers his murdered father’s remains
god_relations.note: Topiltzin recovers or honors Mixcoatl’s bones and establishes mortuary observance.
A Tlaxcalan variant substitutes Coatlicue within Topiltzin’s maternal genealogy.
Disguised Titlacauan shows Topiltzin his decayed appearance and administers intoxicating medicine.
Tezcatlipoca acts as the divine antagonist behind Topiltzin’s humiliation and downfall.
Huitzilopochtli joins the supernatural conspiracy against Topiltzin in Sahagún’s Spanish account.
After Topiltzin’s cremation, his heart rises and manifests as the Morning-Star lord.

Apanecatl.note: Apanecatl and Chimalma are fellow migration leaders or sacred-bundle bearers.
Topiltzin kills Apanecatl, named among his father’s murderers.

Atzcatl Xochtzin.note: Atzcatl Xochtzin is Copil’s daughter and therefore Malinalxochitl’s granddaughter.

Camaxtli.note: Camaxtli is Topiltzin’s father and favors him in the Olmos-derived account.

Centzon Mixcoa.note: After Chimalman's death, they kill Mixcoatl, her child's father.

Chimalcuauhtli.note: One genealogical tradition names Chimalcuauhtli as Copil’s father.

Coyotlinahual.myth: Ruinous sorcery and portents at Tollan
Coyotlinahual.note: Coyotlinahual is a hostile supernatural trickster participating in Tollan’s ruinous portents.

Cuauhcoatl.note: Cuauhcoatl and Chimalma are fellow migration leaders or sacred-bundle bearers.

Cuauhtlequetzqui.myth: Casting Copil’s heart into the reeds
Cuauhtlequetzqui.note: He carries and casts Copil’s extracted heart into the lake.

Cuilton.note: Topiltzin kills Cuilton, a paternal murderer or hostile kinsman.

Ihuimecatl.note: Ihuimecatl brings pulque, sings, and helps intoxicate Topiltzin and Quetzalpetlatl.

Ixcuinanme.note: The Ixcuinanme arrive with captives and inaugurate arrow sacrifice during Huemac’s reign.

Iztaccaltzin.note: Iztaccaltzin appears beside Topiltzin as a fellow or succeeding Toltec monarch.

Iztacmixcoatl.note: Some late chronologies name Iztacmixcoatl as Topiltzin’s father.

Kukulcan.myth: Exiled ruler equated with Maya Feathered Serpent
Kukulcan.note: Colonial and modern histories retrospectively identify Topiltzin with the Maya ruler-deity Kukulcan.

Matlacxochitl.note: Matlacxochitl accompanies or is associated with Topiltzin’s regional flight narrative.

Pochotl.note: Some late Texcocan genealogies present Pochotl as Topiltzin’s descendant.

Quetzalcoatl, the god.note: Topiltzin serves as Quetzalcoatl’s penitential priest and bears the deity’s insignia.
Topiltzin takes the god’s name and becomes difficult to distinguish from him.

Quetzalpetlatl.note: The Anales calls Quetzalpetlatl Topiltzin’s elder sister or ritual counterpart.
Both are intoxicated and implicated together in a euphemistically described sexual transgression.

Tezcacoatl.note: Tezcacoatl and Chimalma are fellow migration leaders or sacred-bundle bearers.

Tlacahuepan.note: Tlacahuepan participates in Sahagún’s divine conspiracy against Topiltzin.

Toltecatl.note: Toltecatl collaborates with Ihuimecatl in the pulque deception that compromises Topiltzin.

Totepeuh.note: Some competing dynastic chronologies make Totepeuh Topiltzin’s father.

Xicomoyahualtzin.note: Reconstructed genealogical material names her as Copil’s consort.
Reconstructed genealogical material names a younger Xicomoyahualtzin as his daughter.

Zolton.note: Topiltzin kills Zolton, a paternal murderer or hostile kinsman.
